title: Applied ML: Quantization Profiles & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Asha Menon
intro: This playbook defines the engineering and evaluation processes we use at Redwood Inference to create, validate, and operate model quantization profiles while maintaining quality guardrails and a clear regression triage workflow. It is intended for ML engineers, inference engineers, SREs, and applied ML reviewers involved in model onboarding and ongoing evaluation.
scope: Applies to all model onboarding and version upgrades that introduce quantized execution (INT8/4-bit/quantized kernels) for models served by Redwood’s runtime. Covers profile creation, offline validation, canary rollout criteria, regression detection, triage steps, and escalation paths.
ownership_and_roles:
- Applied ML (model onboarding): owns evaluation criteria, prompt sets, and quality thresholds.
- Serving Runtime: owns kernel/ops compatibility and performance testing.
- SRE/Platform: owns rollout policies, canary automation, and monitoring.
- Product/CS: provides critical customer prompt sets for high-priority accounts.
Responsibilities must be recorded in the model onboarding ticket and linked to the quantization profile artifact.
quantization_profile_schema:
The quantization profile artifact is a small JSON/YAML file that lists recommended quantization parameters and target kernels. Example schema fields:
- model_name: string (e.g., 'redwood-7b-v2')
- profile_version: semver
- quant_scheme: ['sym','asym','per-channel']
- bitwidth: ['8','4']
- group_size: integer or 'auto'
- fallback_kernels: list of kernel identifiers
- expected_speedup_p50: percent (string)
- expected_latency_delta_p95: percent (string)
- evaluation_prompt_set_id: internal id
- compatibility_notes: free text
A canonical example (JSON snippet):
{
  "model_name": "redwood-7b-v2",
  "profile_version": "1.2.0",
  "quant_scheme": "per-channel",
  "bitwidth": "8",
  "group_size": "auto",
  "fallback_kernels": ["fp16_kernel_v3"],
  "expected_speedup_p50": "+45%",
  "expected_latency_delta_p95": "-10%",
  "evaluation_prompt_set_id": "evalset/redwood-7b-v2/basic-coverage:2026-09-01",
  "compatibility_notes": "Works on Ampere and Hopper; performance on older T4s is reduced."
}
validation_and_thresholds:
Validation should be performed on three layers: offline eval harness, load-tested perf suite, and canary in production. Minimum acceptance criteria (default):
- Quality (automated metrics): BLEU / ROUGE / ROUGE-L / task-specific metrics must not degrade more than 2% relative to FP16 baseline on primary eval set.
- Safety & hallucination checks: no new safety violations in high-confidence outputs; FPR for blocked categories must not increase by more than 0.1 percentage points.
- Latency: p50 latency should improve by >=20% for the quantized path; p95 latency must not worsen by more than 10% compared to FP16 for same batch size.
- Cost: expected per-token CPU/GPU cost reduction documented in profile.
If thresholds are not met, profile is marked 'requires tuning' and falls back to FP16 in rollout until remediated.
offline_evaluation_steps:
1) Create quantization profile artifact and store in model directory.
2) Run eval harness against canonical prompt sets (unit, system, customer-critical) with seed control and deterministic batching.
3) Produce metric diff report versus FP16 baseline: include accuracy-quality metrics, safety flags, and token-level log-likelihood distribution.
4) Run adversarial prompt set (see 'eval-harness adversarial guidance') to detect hallucination regressions.
5) Document failures and propose mitigation: change group_size, switch quant_scheme, disable per-channel, or change kernel.
6) If offline pass succeeds, schedule perf benchmarking on representative hardware nodes (GPU family variants).
Commands (examples):
- run-eval-harness --model model_dir --profile quant/profile-v1.json --prompt-set evalset/redwood-7b-v2/basic-coverage
- perf-benchmark --config tests/perf/latency-p95.yaml --model model_dir --profile quant/profile-v1.json
perf_benchmark_matrix:
Use a matrix of representative hardware and batch sizes. Example table (presented as CSV for portability):
hardware, batch_sizes, expected_p50_delta, expected_p95_delta
hopper-a100-80gb, [1,2,4], +40%, -8%
ampere-a100-40gb, [1,2], +35%, -10%
t4, [1], +5%, +25% (note: T4 often degrades p95)
The profile must include the hardware targets it was validated on and explicitly mark unsupported GPUs.
canary_and_rollout_criteria:
Canary rollout should follow a staged approach:
1) Canary 1: 0.5% traffic, 15 minutes, automated canary health checks pass.
2) Canary 2: 5% traffic, 1 hour, include synthetic end-to-end latency and correctness checks.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% over 6 hours if no regressions detected.
4) Full rollout to 100% by automated policy only when all alerts have remained green for 24 hours.
Automated rollbacks: immediate rollback to FP16 if any of the following triggers fire:
- Quality regression: any customer-critical metric drops by >2% absolute.
- Safety flag increase exceeding thresholds.
- Error budget burn or p95 latency increase >20% sustained for 30 minutes.
Use 'rollout-policy: quantization-canary-v1' in deployment configs.
regression_detection:
We rely on both global metric detectors and targeted prompt set monitors. Detection layers:
- Global aggregated evals (daily regression job).
- Per-customer critical prompt monitors (streaming).
- Canary health checks (latency, error rate, token loss).
Alerting thresholds:
- automated-ticket: generated when aggregated metrics cross thresholds defined in 'validation_and_thresholds'.
- high-priority-pager: generated when customer-critical prompts show >3% regression or safety violations.
Include example alert rule names: 'quant-quality-diff-daily', 'quant-canary-p95-spike', 'quant-customer-critical-failure'.
regression_triage_runbook:
Purpose: Provide a reproducible triage process when a quantization-related regression is detected.
Steps: 1) Triage owner assigns a priority and a primary lead (Applied ML or Runtime engineer).
2) Reproduce locally using the exact model/artifact and quantization profile. Use the eval-harness command with the recorded evalset id.
3) Compare metric diffs and generate a delta report. Attach to the incident ticket.
4) Check kernel compatibility and recent runtime changes (link commit hashes).
5) If regression is quality-related: run ablation by toggling quant params (group_size, per-channel, bitwidth) and re-run targeted prompts to isolate parameter causing degradation.
6) If regression is perf-related: run perf microbenchmarks to determine whether a kernel or batching change caused the p95 spike.
7) Mitigation options: tune profile, pin previous quant profile, or temporarily disable quant path for affected model-version/customer.
8) Postmortem: publish within 3 business days, include decision, timeline, impact table, and follow-up actions.
Escalation path: Applied ML -> Runtime Lead -> SRE Manager -> Head of Product (if customer impact > $50k estimated).
